Legendary graphic designer Susan Kare recently attended the Startup School 2026 event. Her talk has now been uploaded to Y Combinator's YouTube channel — please watch below.

Susan Kare shares fascinating stories and design insights

Over 40 years have passed since the original Macintosh was released, yet its system graphics, fonts, icons, and overall UI elements still look just as brilliant as they did back then.

In fact, many of the elements Susan Kare conceived for the original Macintosh can still be found in macOS today, both in spirit and in literal form. From the Command key symbol, the smiley Mac at startup, the system font, to the hand-shaped cursor — Kare's work not only shaped the visual language of the Mac, but also influenced personal computer design across the entire industry.

Even if you have ever studied the history of Apple, you have likely seen Kare's sketches, or read or listened to her interviews about her early work. Yet every time you hear her recount in person the passion and frustrations from an era when GUI and pixel art were still uncharted territory, it remains thoroughly captivating.

Therefore, if you are interested in design, the history of Apple, or simply enjoy hearing someone talk about the profession they have dedicated their life to and love, Kare's talk is absolutely not to be missed.

In addition to detailing her work at Apple, Kare also talks about how she came to join the company, showcases her work after leaving, shares little anecdotes from Apple's early days, and quotes other legendary designers to bring extra inspiration to the audience.
